tieuDeEn: We are young and our minds are clear and bright – if we don't try hard while it's time to learn, we'll be sorry later. Many people's lives went unfinished not because they weren't clever, but because they were lazy when they were young.

dichXuoi.en: We are young, and our minds are clear and quick to learn. If we don't try hard while it's time to learn, we'll regret it when we grow up.

dichXuoi.en: Look at all the people who leave everything unfinished – it's not because they aren't clever, but because they were lazy and didn't study when they were young.

baiHocEn: Childhood is the best time to learn, while our minds are clear. If we don't try now, we'll regret it later. It's laziness, not a lack of brains, that spoils things.
viecTot: Tuần này, em đặt giờ học cố định mỗi ngày (ví dụ 15 phút đọc sách tiếng Việt) và giữ đúng giờ đó.
en: Cô Hà welcomes you to lesson thirty-one of “Lên Tám” by the poet Tản Đà. Last time we learned that our own hard work is the key to success in learning. Today we'll find out why the ages of eight and ten are the most precious time to learn, and how much we would regret missing it. Sit up nicely and listen.
We are still young, our minds are clear and bright; if we don't try hard when it's time to learn, later we'll be sorry.
Look how many people leave their lives unfinished – it's not because their brains are weak, but because they were lazy and didn't study back then.

The poem reminds us warmly: you are young, your body is growing and your mind is full of energy. “Thanh minh” means very clear and bright, like a sky without a cloud. This is when you learn most easily and remember letters and good values best. The poet warns that if you waste this time and don't try while you are at school, you'll feel sorry later for letting the time slip by.

To prove this, the poem points to real life: many grown-ups look back and feel sorry that things were left unfinished, without a solid career or knowledge. The real reason isn't that they were born less clever – it's that when they were young they were lazy, played too much and didn't try to study. This lesson reminds you to treasure the present and work hard starting today.
